Urinalysis for bilirubin and urobilinogen and urine color: presence of urine bilirubin (conjugated bilirubin) or dark urine supports conjugated/cholestatic or hepatocellular jaundice; absent urine bilirubin favors unconjugated/hemolytic causes.

Specific diagnostic tests: direct antiglobulin test (DAT/Coombs) for autoimmune hemolysis; viral hepatitis serologies (IgM anti-HAV, HBsAg/IgM anti-HBc, HCV RNA) for acute viral hepatitis; abdominal ultrasound (ductal dilation or gallstone) for obstructive jaundice — each will help confirm or exclude the respective candidate.
